math_checks.claim: The 200-person table has aggregate pass rates 68% versus 32% but identical within-stratum rates.
math_checks.recomputation: Users: 64/80=4/5 and 4/20=1/5; nonusers:16/20=4/5 and16/80=1/5. Totals:68/100=17/25 and32/100=8/25; difference9/25=36 percentage points.

math_checks.claim: The same observations allow both a zero-effect world and a world with average effect 136/200.
math_checks.recomputation: In the stipulated zero-effect world set each missing outcome equal to its observed outcome. For the alternative, treated passers68 have Y(1)=1,Y(0)=0; control failures68 have the same pair. Treated failures32 and control passers32 have zero individual effects. Thus136 benefit and64 do not, preserving all observed cells; ATE=136/200=17/25.
math_checks.refutation_attempt: Tried to locate an incompatible observed outcome or a double-counted person; neither exists. The chapter does not infer no effect merely from equal conditional rates.

math_checks.claim: Complete random assignment of 100 out of 200 gives an unbiased difference of group means for the fixed-population ATE.
math_checks.recomputation: Let Z_i indicate treatment. E[Z_i]=1/2; fixed denominators100 give E[sum Z_iY_i(1)/100]=sum Y_i(1)/200. Likewise E[sum(1-Z_i)Y_i(0)/100]=sumY_i(0)/200. Subtraction gives the finite-population ATE. Independence of different Z_i is not required.
math_checks.refutation_attempt: Checked fixed group sizes, expectation over assignment rather than a superpopulation, and the distinction between assignment and actual treatment. These are stated.

math_checks.claim: Standardizing both populations to half stronger and half weaker yields 50% in both arms.
math_checks.recomputation: (1/2)(4/5)+(1/2)(1/5)=1/2. Causal interpretation remains conditional on stated identification assumptions.

recomputation.union_bound: P(any false rejection)≤sum of20 error probabilities≤20×0.0025=0.05

math_checks.claim: Changing target-population weights can change an average treatment effect even with identical stratum effects.
math_checks.recomputation: For stratum effects τ_strong and τ_weak, the population effect is w×τ_strong+(1−w)×τ_weak. Different w can change the result if the stratum effects differ. In the stipulated all-zero-effects world, both terms remain zero for every weight.

math_checks.claim: The four clauses have no satisfying assignment.
Resolution certificate derives y, then not-y, then the empty clause.
math_checks.recomputation: Resolve C1={x,y} with C2={¬x,y} onx to obtain{y}; resolve C3={x,¬y} withC4={¬x,¬y} onx to obtain{¬y}; resolve these on y to obtain the empty set of literals. Clauses use set-like duplicate elimination.

math_checks.claim: The paired SAT clauses exactly exclude monochromatic positive Pythagorean triples.

math_checks.claim: The four-clause toy formula is minimally unsatisfiable.
math_checks.recomputation: Its truth table has exactly one violated clause for each of the four assignments. Removing C1 permits00; removing C2 permits10; removing C3 permits01; removing C4 permits11. Every proper clause subset is therefore satisfiable.

math_checks.claim: The two-case partition on x covers all possibilities and proves contradiction in each branch.
math_checks.recomputation: If x is true, C2 requires y and C4 requires ¬y. If x is false, C1 requires y and C3 requires ¬y. The x/¬x partition is exhaustive.

math_checks.claim: The responses for f:G₀→G₁ and H=r(G₀) are r for challenge0 and r∘f⁻¹ for challenge1.
math_checks.recomputation: The challenge1 map first sends G₁ through f⁻¹ to G₀, then through r to H. For the stated toy maps, r∘f⁻¹ sends a→v,c→u,b→w; both edges map to v—u and u—w, and the unique nonedge maps to v,w. The two table rows are correct.

math_checks.claim: Two accepting responses to the same H yield an isomorphism from G₀ to G₁.
math_checks.recomputation: If φ₀:G₀→H and φ₁:G₁→H are bijective adjacency-preserving maps, then φ₁⁻¹∘φ₀:G₀→G₁ is such a map. In the example this recovers1→a,2→c,3→b.
math_checks.refutation_attempt: Checked the inverse and composition direction, including domains/codomains. No reversal error.

math_checks.claim: False-input soundness is at most1/2 per round even for an unbounded adaptive prover.
math_checks.recomputation: For nonisomorphic G₀,G₁, a fixed H can be isomorphic to at most one of them, since two maps would compose to a forbidden isomorphism. A fresh fair challenge drawn after H is fixed therefore succeeds with probability at most1/2, conditioned on any possible prior transcript.
math_checks.refutation_attempt: Checked that the argument concerns nonisomorphic public graphs, not merely a prover who initially lacks a witness. The chapter explicitly distinguishes these.

math_checks.claim: Twenty sequential rounds have false-acceptance bound2⁻²⁰.

recomputation.chain_rule: P(all20 succeed)=product of conditional round-success probabilities≤(1/2)^20. If any conditioning event has probability zero, the conclusion is immediate.

math_checks.refutation_attempt: Verified the percent conversion, continued conditioning on prior transcripts, commit-before-challenge order, and absence of a reversed posterior-probability claim.

math_checks.claim: The stated simulator exactly reproduces the honest verifier’s view for isomorphic inputs.
math_checks.recomputation: Conditional on b=0, the real response r is uniform over all n! bijections. Conditional on b=1, r∘f⁻¹ is also uniform because composition with fixed f⁻¹ permutes those bijections. In both cases H=response(G_b), and b is uniform. This matches the simulator that chooses b first and then uniform s, outputting(s(G_b),b,s). Graph automorphisms cause no problem because the response map is included in the transcript. Independent fresh choices extend the distribution equality to sequential repetitions.
math_checks.refutation_attempt: Tested the automorphism/multiplicity concern and a malicious challenge chosen as a function of H. The proof handles the former and deliberately restricts its theorem to honest-verifier perfect zero knowledge, without claiming its simple simulator handles the latter.

math_checks.claim: Public transcripts and knowledge extraction have different access guarantees from an honest live verifier.
math_checks.recomputation: A transcript can be fabricated by choosing b before H, including on false inputs; the live false-input prover lacks that order of choice. Extraction needs two valid responses for the same H, requiring a stronger access model such as rewinding. Reusing r gives responses r and r∘f⁻¹, whose inverse-composition (r∘f⁻¹)⁻¹∘r equals f.
math_checks.refutation_attempt: Checked that algebraic special soundness is not falsely presented as a complete efficient knowledge-extractor theorem. Efficiency and success-gap obligations are explicitly retained.

math_checks.claim: NP, IP and PCP measure different resources; a single challenge bit does not mean a constant-bit proof check.
math_checks.recomputation: An explicit graph bijection occupies a number of bits growing with the graph; a direct adjacency check examines all relevant vertex pairs. This remains true even though the verifier chooses only one challenge bit. The chapter separates input reading, proof queries, interaction, prover search and information release.
